newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH EMU OPPONENTS OUTNUMBER SUPPORTERS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH EMU OPPONENTS OUTNUMBER SUPPORTERS - PAPER.

text.p: Finns opposed to membership of European economic and monetary union narrowly outnumbered those in favour in an opinion poll made on behalf of Finnish television news, daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Monday.

It said 43 percent of Finns were opposed and 37 percent in favour. Supporters of the Conservative Party were more pro-EMU than supporters of the other big parties with 61 percent for and 23 percent against, Helsingin Sanomat said.
Of Social Democratic Party supporters, 43 percent viewed EMU favourably and 38 percent negatively. Sixtytwo percent of the opposition Centre Party's supporters were against EMU, it said.

Two thirds of supporters of the Leftist Alliance -- a junior government coalition party -- were opposed to Finnish EMU membership. Among Green Party -- also in the coalition -- voters, 42 percent opposed and 38 percent supported EMU, the paper said.

Full details of the poll could not be obtained immediately since nobody with access to the material was available at the Yleisradio television news or at research institute Taloustutkimus Oy, which made the survey.
An earlier Taloustutkimus poll of almost 2,000 people between January 7 and February 5 found 41 percent of Finns opposed to EMU and 38 percent in favour.
A Suomen Gallup Oy survey of 938 people in February is so far the only opinion poll which has put EMU supporters in the lead; 45 percent in favour and 42 percent opposed.
